policy_title: Improve NHS Dental Access and Sustainability
stated: The Conservative Party's Dental Recovery Plan will unlock 2.5 million more NHS dental appointments through a patient premium, reform the dental contract, require newly qualified dentists to work in the NHS or repay training costs, and promote oral health through 'Smile for Life' and 'golden hellos' for rural dentists.

source.quote: Our Dental Recovery Plan will unlock 2.5 million more NHS dental appointments, through a patient premium to encourage dentists to take on new NHS patients. We will make further reforms to the dental contract to ensure its future sustainability and we will ensure newly qualified dentists have to work in the NHS for a number of years or pay back their training costs.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS dental access and capacity — waiting times, appointment availability, and workforce supply are core healthcare access indicators.

The compulsory NHS-or-repay requirement for newly qualified dentists constrains career choice and affects job security/quality; the contract reform and golden hellos directly move real wages and working conditions for dental professionals.

A 'patient premium' that requires patients to pay an additional charge on top of existing NHS dental bands raises the out-of-pocket cost of a health essential; if structured as a patient co-payment rather than an NHS top-up to dentists, it materially affects the cost of accessing dental care for ordinary households.

Requiring newly qualified dentists to work in the NHS or repay publicly funded training costs is a state coercion mechanism that restricts professional freedom of career choice under financial penalty — a concrete state mandate bearing directly on O10's 'freedom from state coercion' indicator.

membership_note: Three distinct mechanisms justify three bearings: improved healthcare access (O3), potential increase in patient charges for a health essential (O2), and a compulsory-service-or-repayment condition on newly qualified dentists (O10). No material fiscal scale is stated for O12; no direct redistribution mechanism justifies O14; and safety or equality-of-treatment effects are incidental rather than the operative mechanism.
